---
title: "Env.Has"
description: "Check whether a key exists in the Env store."
---

Returns whether any value: of any kind: is associated with `key`.

## Signature

```enforce
static proto native int Has(string key);
```

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| key | `string` | The key to check. |

## Returns

`1` if a value of any kind is associated with `key`, `0` otherwise.

## Behavior

The check is kind-agnostic. `Has` answers whether any value exists for the key, not whether the value has a specific kind. Use it to gate first-run logic when the stored kind does not matter. Combine it with a typed getter, such as [Env.GetInt](./getint), when you need both existence and kind.

## Edge cases

- Returns `0` after [Env.Erase](./erase) or after the key was removed by [Env.Clear](./clear).
- After [Env.SetInt](./setint), [Env.SetBool](./setbool), [Env.SetFloatBits](./setfloatbits), or [Env.SetString](./setstring) on a previously-empty pool, returns `1` regardless of which kind was written.

## Example

```enforce
if (Env.Has("first_run")) {
    Console.Log("returning user");
}
```
